title: Prawn Cocktail
subtitle: Prawns in Marie Rose sauce on a bed of iceberg lettuce
excerpt: The British retro starter that never really went away. Cooked prawns in a sauce of mayonnaise, tomato ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, and lemon, served on shredded iceberg with a wedge of lemon and a slice of brown bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Prawn cocktail became the defining British dinner-party starter from the 1960s through the 1980s. Marie Rose sauce was popularised in Britain by the cook Fanny Cradock in the 1960s. The dish went through a period of derision as shorthand for 1970s unfashionable catering but returned to favour in the 2000s as retro cooking was rehabilitated. It is a genuinely good dish when made with good prawns.

content.text: Prawn cocktail is better than its reputation when made properly. The sauce should have real heat from Tabasco or cayenne, real brightness from lemon juice, and real depth from a small amount of brandy or sherry. Use whole prawns rather than the frozen peeled variety if you can. The iceberg should be very cold and very finely shredded. Serve straight away: the sauce will make the lettuce wilt if it sits.

content.text: Make the Marie Rose sauce: mix the mayonnaise, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, and Tabasco. Taste and adjust: it should be sweet, sharp, and a little spicy. Season with salt and pepper.
Pat the prawns dry with kitchen paper. Add them to the sauce and fold to coat. Taste again and adjust the seasoning.
Arrange the shredded lettuce in 4 glasses or on plates. Spoon the prawns and sauce on top. Dust lightly with paprika and serve with a wedge of lemon and sliced brown bread and butter.
